sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed single-screen arena from a high three-quarter studio camera (threequarter view, pitch 55); Overhead (topdown) as a Settings option
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge handoff v0.85.2 (commit 4390a98, full edition with the arcade module) with 4 small patches; AI Hub session client aihub-session 1.4.0; plain JavaScript in one IIFE; Node 24.22.1 and Playwright 1.63.0 for tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native PS1-style pixel look (320x240 expanded, HD Humanoid rigs, textured TileMap, canvas lighting) dressed as a retro-future TV studio: neon, chrome, marquee bulbs, sponsor logos, confetti, spotlights and a jumbotron
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's procedural rig system (Humanoid and Blob, E.MOVES attacks, poses, flips, landings) plus new motion: the mime's trapped-in-a-box joint post-process, cable drops, boss part tweens, wheel spin easing, TV channel flips
sourceInformation.audio: All synthesized in code: 8 original songs in the engine's notation with layers and 14 stings, about 70 custom sound effects, and Animalese/Simlish Babble voices from a small formant synth for the host, co-host, announcer, bosses, contestants and the crowd
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared-world mode, 1-4 players (the Lightning Round); local co-op 1-4 on one screen
sourceInformation.testing: One command (npm test) runs 20 suites: 18 headless Node suites driving game.advance and game.debug (including room-sweep over all 26 rooms and a scripted playthrough of the whole game) plus 2 Playwright suites: the deliverable over file:// at 1280x720, 1920x1080 and a touch phone, and the AI Hub harness 4 times (2 players; 4 players at 150 ms +-50 ms with 5% loss; host leaving; a server copy) on an in-process 127.0.0.1 server on an OS-picked port. Screenshots only for looks. Finally a full run of the whole game in Chromium driven only by real keyboard and mouse events (no bots in control, no cheats): title to the Season Finale and Ending A (13.6 min), then again collecting the keys: all three episodes, the Green Room, Ending B, credits, initials, Top Earners and back to the title (12.6 min), 0 errors.

testingFeedback: About 16 real issues: contestants could not walk out of exit doors; enemy painters crashed on a missing render state (an error every frame); a missing hpPct field; waves advancing before queued spawns arrived; boss phase coroutines killed by the runner right after their intro (bosses never attacked); the recap and ending scenes keeping flags from the previous visit (the run stalled after Episode 2); a party popper bursting twice; the attract mode's boss reel jumping into the recap; an unseeded Math.random in boss cash; tunings not persisting where storage is absent; the camera fit clamped so the arena was cropped; title menu overlapping the logo; lower third covering the session card buttons; illegible wheel labels. The full real-input run then found a disco ball that could stick in a corner forever (the room could never clear), and the boss bar covering Mashy's head.
5 would be game breaking: no way out of a room after a clear, the per-frame draw crash, bosses that never attacked, the run stalling at the second Prize Recap, and the disco ball stuck in a corner.

The scripted whole-game playthrough (two bots on the left path through all three episodes, the Green Room, Ending B, initials and Top Earners): it found the recap stall and proved every system connects. The room-sweep, which found the boss coroutine bug, was a close second. The full real-input run to the Season Finale was the only test that found the stuck disco ball.

The first version of the enemy-count convergence check in the netcode loopback: it compared one instant of host and client during a spawn burst, so it measured latency rather than mirroring, and had to be rewritten as an average.
engineFeedback: The amount that comes free and works headless: fixed-step game.advance with exact determinism, Humanoid rigs that look good dressed with a few options, the standard pause/settings/controls menus, canvas lighting, and scenes with fades. Writing tests that play the whole game in seconds was easy.

Yes: I assumed the camera fit would land near zoom 1, but the threequarter view's base scale is about 1.5, so my clamp cropped the arena; I guessed r.overlay text glyphs like the multiplication sign and middle dot exist in the tiny font (they don't); and game.addPlayer also fires allowJoin's onJoin, which I didn't expect.

The shared-world netcode (host-authoritative world, client mirror with local prediction, snapshots, claims and hurts) and the boss framework with coroutine phases; also the PlayStation/Xbox glyph icons, since the font has no face-button symbols.
Fitting a fixed single-screen arena to an expanding screen (map.bounds, base view scale and zoom interact), and keeping arrows as aim keys in play while the engine's menus need them to navigate.

Four small patches, each marked MASH TV PATCH: E.HOOKS exposed so presets can switch per player before the Shell reads navigation; the glyphs setting defaulting to PlayStation with an Xbox option applied to every player; E.Arcade initials and continue reading any player's input; and an audio bus getter so the Babble voices obey volume and mute.
A built-in per-player input-preset stack for menus versus play (and face-button glyph icons in the font), so twin-stick games don't need a hook to make arrows aim in play and navigate in menus.

aiHub.name: MASH TV
aiHub.description: A 1-4 player twin-stick arena shooter inside the deadliest game show on TV: blast through studio rooms of goons and robots, grab cash and absurd prizes, keep the ratings up and survive to the Season Finale.
aiHub.controls: WASD/left stick move · mouse/right stick aim & fire · Space/L2 slide · E/R1 Showstopper · Q/L1 Showboat
